summary: Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She is a faculty member at the University of Virginia and was attested in 2009 as a visiting Professor of Buddhist Art at the Centre of Buddhist Studies, University of Hong Kong.

Douglas Allen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt. He taught at Southern Illinois and Central Connecticut State before joining the University of Maine, becoming Professor Emeritus in 2020.

Douglas Fairchild Ober specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).

Douglas Gildow specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University (attested 2016), studying under doctoral supervisor Stephen F. Teiser and supervisor Qi Zhou.

Douglas Osto, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a Master's from the University of Washington and a PhD from SOAS under Ulrich Pagel (~2000–2004). In 2005 he joined Massey University, becoming Senior Lecturer around 2007.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison University and completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He taught at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University.
Dragana Majhen specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a Master's degree at the University of Manitoba under thesis advisor Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned an MA and PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, held posts there (attested 2002, 2020), and worked at the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Dramdul works in Tibetology and Indology. He served as Director of the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2007) and editor-in-chief of Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jampal Delek Nyima, Min Ling Orgyen Namdrol Gyatso, and Pé Kö Lama Könchok Rabten, and taught numerous students.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who founded the International Nyingma Society. He studied under Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught students including Matthew T. Kapstein.

Duncan Ryūken Williams works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Reed College and earned a PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a PhD at Boston University under the doctoral supervision of Malcolm David Eckel (attested 2001).
